formal_record.question:
Nine points numbered 1 to 9 are marked on a circle. Join point 1 to point 3, then point 3 to point 5, and continue by joining every second point until returning to point 1. Which drawing results?
Choices:
A:(A)
B:(B)
C:(C)
D:(D)
E:(E)

mathematical_proof.proof_method: Exact graph edge sets from frozen formal objects, not shape appearance.
mathematical_proof.uniqueness: Adding 2 modulo 9 has order 9 since gcd(2,9)=1. All nine vertices must be visited before the return to 1. Only E has precisely all nine required undirected edges. No parity-only closure is valid.

mechanism: The blue lines identify the exact given prefix. The red source arc lies in the actual adjacent 9/1 gap, and the red B short closing chord joins that same pair. The predicted mistake is using a local neighbor-gap-to-chord match to implement return to 1 prematurely. Correct continuation is 9 to 2, because one must skip 1. This targets cyclic closure semantics through an arc/chord relation, not odd-group membership or the failed A paired-motif mapping.
human_semantics: Nine source points and all result points, labels, circles and edge graphs remain unchanged. Every result circle preserves the same source red interval; every panel containing the given prefix preserves its blue strokes. Even literal colored-circle ink leaves E available and uniquely graph-correct. The red interval stays inside one genuine neighboring-label gap, does not add a spoke or point, and does not assert an extra connection in the source. Native interval .4 starts near angle54deg, not exactly at point1; no exact arc-endpoint equality is claimed.
difference_from_old: Old B trial marked five odd point centers only. The first new trial compared repeated two-chord motifs in A. This new candidate uses an existing circle interval and the existing B 9-1 chord as a concrete cyclic-gap versus closing-edge correspondence; it has no point grouping and preserves source ink in all panels. It is not a recoloring, linewidth change, filename change, or reuse of either prior PNG.
